What is the difference between a day spa and a medical spa?

A day spa is about relaxation, with treatments like massages and basic facials. A medical spa offers treatments that change the skin itself, such as injectables, microneedling and chemical peels, and they're provided by licensed medical providers after a medical assessment.
Who will be performing my treatments?

Brooke, our nurse practitioner injector, does every injection. Abby, our medical aesthetician and senior laser technician, looks after facials and skin treatments. You'll know who is treating you before your appointment.

The treatments we offer are well established and, in trained hands, carry a low risk of side effects. We check your medical history first, go through the risks of your treatment at your consultation, and tell you if something isn't right for you.
What should I expect during my initial consultation?

We'll ask what you'd like to change, go through your medical history and look at your skin. You'll leave with a written plan and a quote. Your first consultation can be in person or by video, and whether you start that day is up to you.
Do treatments like Botox or filler hurt?
Most people describe a quick pinch. The needles are very fine, most fillers contain a local anesthetic, and we can apply numbing cream first if you'd like.
How long do the results of Botox and dermal fillers last?
Botox usually lasts three to four months. Dermal fillers last six to eighteen months, depending on the product and where it's placed.
Is there any downtime after a procedure?

Often none. You can go straight back to your day after Botox, a HydraFacial or dermaplaning. Fillers can leave some swelling or bruising for a few days, and Morpheus8 and deeper peels need a few days more. Each treatment's page lists its downtime.
How much do medical spa treatments cost?

It depends on the treatment and how much you need, so we quote at your consultation, before anything is done. Our membership is $149 a month and includes a monthly facial and 10% off treatments, and financing is available through Cherry and CareCredit.

props.text: About fifteen minutes, no anesthetic and no downtime. Placed by our nurse practitioner, who usually starts with fewer units than you'd expect.
Pricing depends on the number of units and the areas treated. You'll get a quote at your consultation.

Botox is botulinum toxin type A, a purified protein that temporarily relaxes the muscle it's placed in. Small amounts in the upper face stop those muscles from creasing the skin, so the lines they cause soften.

It doesn't fill, tighten or remove anything. A line you can still see when your face is completely relaxed is etched into the skin, and Botox alone will only improve it slowly. That's the first thing your provider checks.
What it can do for you
Most people describe how they look rather than what they want done: tired, annoyed, older than they feel. In the upper face, that usually comes down to three muscles.
Forehead lines soften without dropping your brow.
The frown line between your eyebrows stops making you look cross.
Crow's feet ease when you smile.
A heavy brow can lift slightly when the muscle pulling it down relaxes.
Most healthy adults are good candidates. Your consultation is where we confirm that and work out how much you need. For a first treatment, it's usually less than you'd think.

You're pregnant or breastfeeding, have a neuromuscular condition, have an infection where you'd be treated, or your lines are static. In that last case, your provider may suggest a skin treatment or filler instead.

All four are botulinum toxin type A. They differ in how quickly they start, how far they spread and how they behave over years of treatment. Having all four means your provider can choose the one that suits you.

The needle is very fine and each injection takes about a second. Most patients describe a quick sting. No anesthetic is needed, and you can drive yourself home.
How soon will I see Botox results?
Movement starts to soften after three to seven days, and the full effect shows at about two weeks. We book your follow-up then.
Will Botox make me look frozen?
Not if it's dosed and placed well. We treat the muscles that are creasing the skin and leave the rest working, and we keep first treatments conservative.
What happens when Botox wears off?
Your muscles gradually go back to how they worked before, and so do the lines. Nothing ends up worse than it was.
How many units of Botox will I need?
It depends on your muscles and the areas you want treated, so we can't say over the phone. You'll get your number and a quote after the assessment, before anything is injected.

Dr. Stone is the visionary leader of Stone Surgical Arts, Stone Dental Implant Center and Westlake Medical Aesthetics. With unrivaled expertise, she's committed to artistic surgical excellence and patient well-being.
What is the difference between a day spa and a medical spa?

A day spa is about relaxation, with treatments like massages and basic facials. A medical spa offers treatments that change the skin itself, such as injectables, microneedling and chemical peels, and they're provided by licensed medical providers after a medical assessment.
Who will be performing my treatments?

Brooke, our nurse practitioner injector, does every injection. Abby, our medical aesthetician and senior laser technician, looks after facials and skin treatments. You'll know who is treating you before your appointment.

The treatments we offer are well established and, in trained hands, carry a low risk of side effects. We check your medical history first, go through the risks of your treatment at your consultation, and tell you if something isn't right for you.
What should I expect during my initial consultation?

We'll ask what you'd like to change, go through your medical history and look at your skin. You'll leave with a written plan and a quote. Your first consultation can be in person or by video, and whether you start that day is up to you.
Do treatments like Botox or filler hurt?
Most people describe a quick pinch. The needles are very fine, most fillers contain a local anesthetic, and we can apply numbing cream first if you'd like.
How long do the results of Botox and dermal fillers last?
Botox usually lasts three to four months. Dermal fillers last six to eighteen months, depending on the product and where it's placed.
Is there any downtime after a procedure?

Often none. You can go straight back to your day after Botox, a HydraFacial or dermaplaning. Fillers can leave some swelling or bruising for a few days, and Morpheus8 and deeper peels need a few days more. Each treatment's page lists its downtime.
How much do medical spa treatments cost?

It depends on the treatment and how much you need, so we quote at your consultation, before anything is done. Our membership is $149 a month and includes a monthly facial and 10% off treatments, and financing is available through Cherry and CareCredit.
